g.text: Residue of the N-terminal domain, numbered as in the structure file
Predicted aligned error (PAE) of a contact in Å: written from 5 Å, bold from 10 Å. Not pLDDT
Stroke weight and opacity follow the model's pLDDT: a contact is drawn at the lower of its two ends'
values, a residue at its own. ? marks pLDDT below 50.
The atoms that are drawn of a residue are all at their residue's pLDDT: this model gives one value for a
residue, not one for each of its atoms.
An interface has no centre. The residues of the N-terminal domain that touch the C-terminal domain
stand in a column, as boxes, in the order of the sequence; a dotted line stands for residues in between
that do not; those of the C-terminal domain around it. A line is a pair of residues, at the shortest of its
Where a residue of the N-terminal domain makes a contact that has a direction (an H-bond, a salt bridge
and the like), the atoms that make it are drawn beside its box, and with them its backbone nitrogen and
carbonyl. The box is the residue's alpha carbon. A line that ends on such an atom is the contact of that
atom and gives its distance; a line that ends on a box stands for the pair of residues.
All 2 residues of the N-terminal domain at the interface are shown, with 5 contacts.
PAE (predicted aligned error) is the model's expected error, in ångström, in placing one residue of a
contact relative to the other: low is confident, about 32 means no idea. It is not pLDDT, which line weight,
All 4 residue pairs in contact have a PAE of 5 Å or more, written on their lines.
